summary: Compute Graph is a node-based GPU framework for RealityKit particle simulations, introduced in macOS 27 and tied to RealityKit and Reality Composer Pro. BifrOSt has a GPU presenter (springboard/src/gpu/) for compositing, not a particle or node-graph simulation framework, and no RealityKit counterpart.

features.note: Builds and compiles a node graph into Metal pipelines. BifrOSt's GPU code (springboard/src/gpu/) is fixed compositing shaders, not user-defined graphs.
Typed node ports and operations. No equivalent exists in the BifrOSt SDK.

features.apple: element, emitter, initialize, module, output, force
features.note: Particle lifecycle stages. Not in BifrOSt.

features.apple: graph, group, texture, random, matrix4x4f, matrix4x4h
features.note: Helper nodes for time, sampling and transforms. Not in BifrOSt.
Per-frame GPU advance and element spawn, bound to Metal command buffers. BifrOSt uses OpenGL/EGL on Linux.
3D simulation inputs for RealityKit scenes. BifrOSt has no 3D scene graph.

gaps: None that fits a macOS-style desktop. A node-based particle framework would be a 3D engine feature outside the desktop's scope.
